disclaimer: Synthetic triage rules written for a hackathon demonstration. Adapted in spirit from publicly described triage frameworks (Emergency Severity Index, Manchester Triage System discriminators). NOT clinically validated and NOT for real patient care.

urgency_levels.HIGH: Urgent assessment. Must be seen ahead of routine attendances.
urgency_levels.MODERATE: Standard assessment within the normal departmental queue.
urgency_levels.LOW: Routine assessment. No time-critical feature identified.

rules.rationale: Chest pain accompanied by breathing difficulty is treated as a potential cardiac or pulmonary emergency until a clinician excludes one.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - cardiac pain with dyspnoea discriminator

rules.rationale: Chest pain radiating to the arm, jaw, neck or back is a recognised feature of acute coronary syndrome and requires urgent assessment.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - cardiac pain discriminator

rules.rationale: Chest pain with sweating and nausea together form an autonomic pattern associated with acute coronary events.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - cardiac pain discriminator

rules.rationale: Chest pain with loss of consciousness suggests haemodynamic compromise and is time-critical.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - level 1 high-risk presentation

rules.rationale: Severe chest pain, reported at 7 or above out of 10, warrants urgent assessment regardless of other features.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - severe pain discriminator

rules.rationale: Chest pain in a patient with known cardiac disease carries a materially higher pre-test probability of a cardiac cause.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - high-risk history

rules.rationale: New chest pain within the last twelve hours in a patient aged 40 or over is treated as possible acute coronary syndrome pending assessment.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - age-weighted cardiac risk

rules.rationale: Chest pain that worsens on breathing, together with fever, points towards a respiratory rather than cardiac cause and can follow the standard pathway.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - pleuritic pain pattern

rules.rationale: Mild chest wall pain reproducible on pressure, with no dyspnoea and no radiation, is consistent with a musculoskeletal cause. Note that every cardiac feature must be explicitly excluded before this rule can fire.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - chest wall pain pattern

rules.rationale: Fever with neck stiffness is treated as possible meningitis, which is time-critical.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - meningism discriminator

rules.rationale: A non-blanching rash with fever is treated as possible meningococcal sepsis and cannot wait.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - purpuric rash discriminator

rules.rationale: Altered mental state with fever is a recognised marker of sepsis or central nervous system infection.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - altered mental status

rules.rationale: A temperature of 40 degrees Celsius or above is a hyperpyrexia threshold requiring urgent assessment.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - very hot discriminator

rules.rationale: Fever with breathing difficulty suggests a lower respiratory tract infection with respiratory compromise.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - respiratory distress with infection

rules.rationale: Fever in an immunocompromised patient may represent neutropenic sepsis and is treated as urgent regardless of how well the patient appears.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - high-risk immunosuppression

rules.rationale: A fever persisting five days or more warrants assessment for a cause but has no time-critical feature.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - prolonged fever

rules.rationale: A short-lived low-grade fever with no red-flag feature follows the routine pathway. Each red flag must be explicitly excluded, not merely unmentioned.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - uncomplicated febrile illness

rules.rationale: Inability to complete a sentence in one breath indicates severe respiratory distress.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - unable to talk in sentences

rules.rationale: Visible cyanosis with breathing difficulty indicates significant hypoxia.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - cyanosis discriminator

rules.rationale: Sudden breathlessness with chest pain is treated as possible pulmonary embolism or pneumothorax.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - level 1 high-risk presentation

rules.rationale: An asthmatic patient with active wheeze and breathlessness may be in an acute exacerbation, which can deteriorate quickly.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - acute asthma pathway

rules.rationale: Breathlessness with fever suggests pneumonia or another infective respiratory cause with systemic involvement.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - respiratory infection with distress

rules.rationale: Breathlessness present for a week or more, with speech intact and no cyanosis or chest pain, is a chronic presentation suitable for the standard respiratory pathway.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - chronic breathlessness

rules.rationale: Bleeding that cannot be controlled by direct pressure is immediately life-threatening.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - exsanguinating haemorrhage

rules.rationale: Head injury with any loss of consciousness requires immediate assessment for intracranial injury.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - head injury with reduced consciousness

rules.rationale: Head injury in a patient taking anticoagulants carries a substantially raised risk of delayed intracranial bleeding, even when the patient currently appears well.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - anticoagulation as a high-risk modifier

rules.rationale: A high-energy mechanism such as a road traffic collision or a fall from height can conceal serious injury behind an unremarkable initial appearance.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - mechanism of injury

rules.rationale: Visible limb deformity indicates probable fracture or dislocation needing prompt orthopaedic assessment.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - obvious deformity

rules.rationale: Inability to bear weight after a limb injury warrants imaging but carries no immediate threat.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - weight-bearing assessment

rules.rationale: A minor injury with no bleeding, no head involvement, no deformity and preserved function follows the routine pathway.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - minor limb injury

rules.rationale: A rigid abdomen suggests peritonitis, which is a surgical emergency.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - peritonism discriminator

rules.rationale: Vomiting blood indicates active upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - haematemesis

rules.rationale: Black tarry stool indicates gastrointestinal bleeding that has already occurred and may be ongoing.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - melaena

rules.rationale: Abdominal pain in pregnancy requires urgent obstetric input; ectopic pregnancy and placental complications are time-critical.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - abdominal pain in pregnancy

rules.rationale: Abdominal pain that begins suddenly and is severe may indicate perforation, obstruction or vascular catastrophe.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - severe pain of sudden onset

rules.rationale: Lower abdominal pain with testicular pain raises the possibility of testicular torsion, where delay costs the testis.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - testicular pain discriminator

rules.rationale: Abdominal pain with fever suggests an inflammatory or infective cause such as appendicitis and needs surgical assessment.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - abdominal pain with pyrexia

rules.rationale: Mild abdominal pain with every red-flag feature explicitly excluded follows the routine pathway.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - uncomplicated abdominal pain

rules.rationale: A patient returning within 72 hours with the same unresolved complaint is a recognised marker of a missed or deteriorating condition, and is reviewed by a clinician regardless of how the presentation scores on its own.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - unscheduled re-presentation

rules.rationale: Older patients frequently under-report symptom severity and deteriorate with fewer warning signs, so moderate or worse pain in this group is reviewed by a clinician.
rules.source: Emergency Severity Index - age as a high-risk modifier

rules.rationale: Significant pain during pregnancy requires obstetric assessment that this rule set is not equipped to provide.
rules.source: Manchester Triage System - pregnancy as a high-risk modifier
